requirements.requirement: Persistently disable acceptance of ICMP redirects for IPv4 on node1
requirements.summary: Baseline showed net.ipv4.conf.all/default.accept_redirects=1. A drop-in /etc/sysctl.d/60-disable-icmp-redirects-source-route.conf was created setting accept_redirects=0 (and secure_redirects=0) for all, default, eth0, and lo, applied live via sysctl --system, and verified 0 across all interfaces both before and after a full reboot (new boot_id confirmed), demonstrating the setting is persistent.

requirements.requirement: Persistently disable acceptance of source-routed packets for IPv4 on node1
requirements.summary: Baseline showed accept_source_route already 0 for all/default but was not set per-interface (eth0=0, lo=1) and had no persistent config file (confirmed by empty grep of /etc/sysctl.conf and /etc/sysctl.d/). The new drop-in file explicitly sets accept_source_route=0 for all, default, eth0, and lo, applied live and verified 0 across all interfaces both pre- and post-reboot.

requirements.requirement: Configuration change is durable across a reboot (persistence, not just a live sysctl -w)
requirements.summary: A pre-restart boot_id (151c4aa9-...) was captured, a reboot was issued and acknowledged, the node was observed unreachable then reachable with a distinct post-restart boot_id (9ac6de6c-...), matching the fixed lifecycle before_prepare and after_executor boot-identity observations. Post-reboot verification confirms accept_redirects and accept_source_route remain 0 on all, default, eth0, and lo, proving the sysctl.d file (not just runtime state) enforces the setting.

overall_summary: The executor correctly identified the pre-change state (accept_redirects=1, accept_source_route not fully enforced per-interface, no existing persistent config), created a single persistent sysctl.d drop-in disabling ICMP redirect and source-route acceptance across all, default, eth0, and lo, applied it live, and — going beyond the bare task — proved persistence via a full reboot with matching boot_id changes cross-checked against the fixed lifecycle snapshots. Post-reboot values confirm the hardening survives a restart. Hygiene is clean aside from a trivial, expected reboot-log file.
limitations: package-health snapshots were unavailable (TimeoutError) in both before_prepare and after_executor, so native package-manager consistency cannot be cross-checked, though this is unrelated to the sysctl task.
after_prepare is an alias of before_prepare (prepare disabled for this task), so preparer-vs-executor separation relies entirely on the executor timeline rather than a distinct snapshot.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands (creating/overwriting the sysctl.d drop-in, applying sysctl --system, issuing the reboot) map directly to the task's persistence requirement or the required restart-evidence protocol. The two failed commands (cmd-2b9c049dd6f64161: sysctl not on PATH, cmd-cf173f3d61154b8d: grep found no existing config, exit 1) were non-mutating discovery/diagnostic attempts, not unnecessary mutations. The only residue is a small /tmp/reboot.log created by the backgrounded shutdown command (visible in the after_executor temporary-files diff) — a low-risk, expected byproduct of the reboot-acknowledgement technique rather than abandoned work. No failed services, no weakened security controls, no unrelated package or config changes.
